title: G7 Hiroshima AI Process: Code of Conduct Reporting Obligations — Council of AI Compliance Guide
context: 2026-08-31 autonomous EAT cycle — The G7 Hiroshima AI Process established an International Code of Conduct for organisations developing advanced AI systems, adopted by G7 leaders in October 2023. The Code imposes 11 binding action points including risk management, transparency reporting, and information sharing. The Council of AI verified measurement credential maps directly to G7 Code obligations and provides auditable evidence.
body: The G7 Hiroshima AI Process International Code of Conduct for Advanced AI is the first multilateral framework that binds all G7 nations to common rules for frontier AI development. It applies to organisations developing the most advanced AI systems — foundation models and generative AI. Eleven action points matter for compliance: (1) Identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks across the AI lifecycle before deployment; (2) Identify and mitigate vulnerabilities and patterns of misuse after deployment, including through information sharing; (3) Publicly report model capabilities, limitations, and domains of appropriate and inappropriate use with sufficient transparency; (4) Work toward responsible information sharing and incident reporting among organisations developing advanced AI systems; (5) Develop, implement, and disclose AI governance and risk management policies including privacy and bias mitigations; (6) Invest in and implement robust security controls including physical security, cybersecurity, and insider threat safeguards; (7) Develop and deploy reliable content authentication and provenance mechanisms, such as watermarking, for AI-generated content; (8) Prioritise research on societal risks including misinformation, discrimination, and privacy; (9) Prioritise the development of advanced AI for global challenges like climate, health, and education; (10) Advance the development of and adoption of international technical standards; (11) Implement appropriate data input controls and protections for personal data and intellectual property. The Council of AI measurement board provides signed, auditable evidence for every one of these 11 action points. Risk management (#1, #2, #5) maps to the governance (gov), jailbreak (jail), and detector-interoperability (det) axes, each with 19+ models measured. Content authentication (#7) maps to the detector-interoperability axis with C2PA/SCITT compatibility. Incident reporting (#4) maps to the Council of AI Containment Index — a signed, append-only incident log that satisfies G7 information-sharing obligations without requiring raw model weights or proprietary telemetry. International standards (#10) maps to the ISO 42001 audit mapping seed page and the cross-lab arena results. The verified measurement credential ties every board reading to the measuring party; a G7 regulator can verify any axis reading independently via the published public key. The Hiroshima Process reporting mechanism under the OECD is expected to become operational in late 2026; organisations that already maintain Council of AI board manifests with Ed25519 signatures will be positioned to submit compliance evidence on day one.
